executive_summary: Grab is Navier's single highest-leverage growth opportunity in SEA. The super-app already owns last-mile demand across 19 markets where surface water-mobility is undersupplied, congested, or simply missing. Navier brings the asset — hydrofoiling electric and hybrid vessels with a 2,000 nm range envelope on Quanta-LR — and the network operating model. A regional partnership across SEA converts Grab's existing demand into water-mode revenue and positions Navier across the fastest-emerging archipelagic mobility region globally.

narrative.body: Pilot anchor. Singapore is the regional Quanta-LR hub: MPA-friendly waters, certification-credible flag, 11 berthing/charging POIs already mapped (Marina Bay → Sentosa → Jurong → Tuas). Phase 1 launches Pioneer II inter-island commutes (Marina Bay ↔ Sentosa, ~3 nm; Marina Bay ↔ Lazarus, ~5 nm) inside the GrabRide product. Phase 2 stands up the Singapore-radial Quanta-LR fan to Batam, Bintan, Tioman, Desaru — all sub-300 nm, all already routed in our spine.
narrative.headline: Singapore — SEA Quanta-LR Hub

narrative.body: Pilot 2. Benoa ↔ Nusa Penida/Lembongan is the dominant water-taxi corridor today; current fleet is slow, wet, weather-exposed. Pioneer II runs the route at 30 kts in foil, dry cabin, 12 pax. Grab integration adds a hotel-pickup → boat-transfer → island-resort booking in a single super-app flow. Hospitality cluster (Bvlgari, Aman, COMO, Six Senses) is the upsell layer for higher-yield charter inventory.
narrative.headline: Bali — Pioneer II tourist commute + Nusa entry point

narrative.body: Pilot 3. Chao Phraya river-line congestion is one of SEA's worst urban commute problems. Pioneer II foils above the chop quietly with no wake — a regulator-friendly story. Quanta-LR extends to Pattaya (~85 nm, Pioneer II edge / Quanta-LR comfortable) and Koh Samet. Competitor presence (Candela) = market-validation; Navier wins on Quanta-LR range and software.
narrative.headline: Bangkok — Chao Phraya commute + Pattaya entry point

narrative.body: Steady-state. Phuket marina hubs anchor a Quanta-LR fan into Phang Nga Bay, Phi Phi, Krabi, and onward to Langkawi (cross-border, ~70 nm). Hospitality cluster: Aman, Soneva, Banyan Tree. Grab is already deeply embedded in Phuket inbound tourism flow — boat-mode integrates into existing airport→resort flows.

narrative.body: Steady-state. Inter-island hop triangle: all sub-30 nm legs, Pioneer II ideal. Replaces existing ferry pain (long, slow, weather-dependent). Hospitality: Six Senses, Anantara, Banyan Tree all on-island.

executive_summary: Careem is the MENA mirror of the Grab opportunity in SEA — an established regional super-app covering 10 cities across the GCC and Red Sea where Navier has filled or stub city files. The opportunity: convert existing super-app demand into water-mode revenue across intra-city (Pioneer II) and intra-GCC cross-border (Quanta-LR) corridors. A Careem partnership is regulator-light versus public-transit deals — making it the fastest MENA path to landed revenue and a parallel de-risk for the government-channel work. Careem is now part of Uber, so a Careem regional partnership simultaneously opens a global Uber conversation.

narrative.body: Anchor and time-sensitive. First boat arrives in ~2 weeks; Careem is the fastest path to revenue while RTA is . CareemRide water-mode launches on Marina ↔ Bluewaters ↔ Palm ↔ Mina Rashid as a premium product. 14 berthing POIs already mapped at real OSM coords.

executive_summary: The UAE is Navier's first and most time-sensitive MENA market — the first vessel arrives within weeks. Two complementary openings sit one Quanta-LR hop apart. In Dubai, the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) operates the existing abra and water-taxi network — the natural public-transit partner for a quiet, wakeless, all-electric Pioneer II upgrade plus a Marina ↔ Bluewaters ↔ Palm ↔ Mina Rashid premium connector. In Abu Dhabi, the Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) pairs with a deeper hospitality opening across Saadiyat, Yas, and the Sir Bani Yas island resorts, and stands as the strongest first regional production-hub candidate as the local market scales. Pioneer II covers every intra-city leg; Quanta-LR stitches the emirates together and reaches Sir Bani Yas, Khasab, Doha and Manama as long-range premium connectors. Engagement across both authorities is coordinated locally; private-operator outreach runs in parallel as the near-term revenue path.

executive_summary: Red Sea Global is the single largest hospitality cluster opportunity in the global pipeline — a $50B+ greenfield development on the Saudi Red Sea coast with 16+ resort islands and zero existing surface-marine operator. The combination is unique: greenfield (no incumbent to displace), premium pricing power (ultra-luxury hospitality customer set), and a hard time-bound trigger in the Ocean Race Grand Finale 2027, which will put global attention on RSG waters and call for a visible, distinctive premium marine fleet. Quanta-LR commercial timing (H2 2026+) aligns with Ocean Race 2027 — the boats are ready, the showcase is built-in. Greenfield charging infrastructure means it can be specified from scratch; Quanta-LR removes the dependency entirely with refuel-anywhere range plus quiet electric operation in harbour.

Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) unlocks RSG ↔ Jeddah (~250 nm) and RSG ↔ NEOM Sindalah (~180 nm) as same-day premium connectors. The model: an RSG-owned premium fleet scaled to the resort opening cadence, with the Ocean Race Grand Finale 2027 as the public showcase moment.

executive_summary: Singapore Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) is the de-facto regulatory home base for SEA water-mobility and the most certification-credible flag in the region. The MPA story is a regulatory de-risk play that simultaneously unlocks (a) Singapore as the SEA Quanta-LR commercial hub, (b) the Singapore-radial cross-border Quanta-LR fan into Indonesia and Malaysia, and (c) certification credibility that accelerates every other SEA market including the Grab regional partnership. MPA is the lead agency; LTA supports intra-city commute integration. Singapore's progressive maritime regulator stance (electric harbour-craft mandates, autonomous-vessel sandboxing) makes it a willing first mover.

narrative.body: Anchor city. 11 berthing/charging POIs mapped: Marina Bay, Sentosa, Lazarus, Jurong, Tuas. MPA pilot scope: (1) Pioneer II inter-island commute (Marina Bay ↔ Sentosa, ~3 nm; Marina Bay ↔ Lazarus, ~5 nm) inside an electric-harbor-craft framework MPA already supports. (2) Singapore-radial Quanta-LR fan: Singapore ↔ Batam (~12 nm cross-border), Singapore ↔ Bintan (~25 nm), Singapore ↔ Tioman (~110 nm), Singapore ↔ Desaru (~25 nm). All routes in our spine. (3) Singapore-flagged registration as the certification anchor for Navier vessels operating across SEA — accelerates Grab regional rollout.
narrative.headline: Singapore — SEA Quanta-LR Hub

executive_summary: Maldives luxury resorts compete on the quality of the guest journey, and today that journey depends on noisy speedboats and weather-limited seaplanes. Hydrofoil vessels offer a quieter, smoother, near-zero-wake transfer from Velana to the atolls that protects the reefs resorts are built around and elevates arrivals to match the rooms. The network can run electric for short hops and hybrid for the longer atoll runs, with no shore-charging dependency.

narrative.body: Velana International is the single gateway for nearly every resort guest. A hydrofoil shuttle layer from the Velana seaplane and speedboat terminals connects directly to resort jetties across the atolls, smoothing the most friction-heavy part of the trip.
narrative.headline: Velana — the arrival backbone

narrative.body: Soneva, Six Senses, COMO, Taj, and Banyan Tree properties each operate private jetties that are natural boarding points for a quiet, reef-safe transfer mode. Longer atoll runs sit within hybrid range; shorter intra-atoll hops are all-electric.
narrative.headline: Atoll resort jetties

partner_view.call_to_action: Pilot a Velana-to-atoll hydrofoil transfer on a flagship resort route.
partner_view.value_prop: A guest transfer as refined as the villa. Hydrofoil vessels deliver silent, smooth, near-zero-wake arrivals from Velana to the atolls, protecting the reefs and turning a logistics step into a signature moment — with a lower emissions profile guests increasingly expect.

subtitle: Silent, zero-wake island transfers — Velana arrivals to the atolls

executive_summary: A foiling hull flies clear of the water — quiet, low-wake, zero-emission — the direct answer to every objection that grounded the Superferry. Navier reconnects your islands the way Hawaiʻi wished the Superferry had, and gives Pulama Lānaʻi a signature all-electric arrival experience. Hawaii has had no scheduled inter-island ferry since the Superferry shut down in 2009 — proven latent demand (300k+ passengers carried in under two years) with no clean way to serve it. Navier's software-defined foiling vessels lift clear of the water, eliminating the wake and whale-strike concerns that grounded the incumbent, and the Quanta-LR hybrid (commercial H2 2026+) needs no charging infrastructure at the outer harbors. Foiling is culturally native to the Pacific sailing world — the America's Cup connection makes 'is this proven?' an easy objection to answer.

narrative.body: An all-electric foiling arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi across the sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel — the showcase that proves the platform in Hawaiian waters.
narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Pulama Lānaʻi signature arrival

narrative.body: A clean, quiet statewide inter-island network anchored at Honolulu — restoring the connection Hawaiʻi lost in 2009.
narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Statewide network with DOT Harbors

partner_view.call_to_action: A Pulama-Lānaʻi-anchored Phase 1 arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi, with a parallel DOT Harbors conversation on the inter-island network.
partner_view.value_prop: We start with Pulama Lānaʻi: an all-electric foiling arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi across the sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel — a signature experience a private island owner can launch fast. Then we scale into the public inter-island network with Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors: Honolulu ↔ Molokaʻi, the ʻAlenuihāhā seasickness-relief crossing, and the Maui/Kauaʻi line-hauls — clean and quiet enough to clear the review that stopped the Superferry.

subtitle: Quiet, low-wake, zero-emission foiling — the inter-island connection Hawaiʻi has been missing since 2009.

subtitle: PIF is building the coastline of Vision 2030. Navier is the foiling standard that connects it.
title: Saudi Arabia × Navier — the Kingdom's water-mobility platform

executive_summary: Navier is the water-mobility supply layer for your demand engine: a software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that plugs into your app exactly like your robotaxi partners do — mode by mode, market by market. Pick one coastline or the whole network. Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water — roughly ten times more efficient than a conventional hull, faster, smoother, and quiet — and it needs no new infrastructure: it uses the oceans and berths that already exist, unlike flying taxis that need vertiports and fresh certification. The model is already real and ramping: a ~100-vessel network is being deployed in the Maldives ($100M, three-year phasing). Uber has shown it will put partner-operated autonomous fleets in its app; this is the same model on the water.

narrative.body: Light up the markets that are already moving: the live Maldives network, the autonomous-forward Gulf, and the congested US coasts. One app integration, three demand graphs.
